A comment line is ignored by the client parser, so a comment keepalive fixes the bytes and not the visibility — the one consumer that needs to see it is the only one specified to ignore it. The skeleton's idle and dead streams are byte-identical (AST-0034), which is what REQ-0018's second clause forbids. ⚠️ RECONNECTION IS ITSELF A CHANGE HINT. Because events are hints and never deltas (#73), a reconnecting client that reloads is exactly caught up — so no event buffer, no `id:` field and no `Last-Event-ID` handling are needed. This is the one place in the design where the contract removes work rather than adding it. ⚠️ A WATCHER FAILURE EMITS A VISIBLE SIGNAL OR CLOSES THE STREAM. Logging alone is forbidden: the operator is looking at a browser, and a logged failure with a live-looking page is the retained-workspace-reported-destroyed defect exactly.
responsibility: Keep every open view current: watch the content root, emit a named heartbeat event carrying data at a fixed interval, deliver change notifications as hints, and run the client watchdog that renders a visibly disconnected state when a heartbeat does not arrive.
